psycho_education: P: Therapist provided psycho-education (e.g., directive education about the traumatic event, normal reactiosn to trauma, etc.; education to instill hope)
psycho_education_general: General info re: abuse, trauma; specific info re: trauma child experienced (GE) and the child's reactions to his/her personal experience of the trauma
psycho_education_common_responses: Common emotional, behavioral, and physiological responses.
psycho_education_symptoms: Info about child's symptoms and diagnosis.
psycho_education_components: Description of components of TF-CBT, session structure, treatment length
psycho_education_engaged_family: Engaged family (e.g., found out what child liked, what motivates the family, etc.)
parenting_skills: P: Therapist provided parenting skills (e.g., praise, selective attention, time out, bx mng plans); ask parent about their reactions to the child's traumatic experience
relaxation: R: Therapist explained the physiology of relaxation and rationale for relaxation techniques; instructed on methods of relaxation
relaxation_trauma_help: Discuss ways that relaxation skills can help child with trauma reactions (GE); suggest that child use relaxation skills when they have trauma reminders
affect: A: Therapist assisted child in accurately identifying their feelings, and various ways of regulating their emotions (e.g., imagery, thought stopping, positive self-talk)
affect_express_feelings: Accurately identify and express a variety of feelings (positive and negative, in youth's words) (e.g. feelings brainstorm, Color My World, etc.)
affect_link_feelings: Link feelings to situations, body and facial expressions
affect_rate_emotions: Teach how to rate intensity levels of emotions (e.g. SUDS, feeling thermometer)
affect_manage_emotions: Teach skills of managing emotions and difficult affective states (e.g. positive self-talk, enhancing child's sense of safety, etc.)
affect_cope_feelings: Teach skills to identify/cope with array of feelings associated with trauma (GE)
cognitive_coping: C: Therapist reviewed skill of cognitive coping
cognitive_coping_educate: Educate child on the distinction and relationship between thoughts, feelings and actions (e.g. acknowledge internal dialogues; introduce cognitive triangle)
cognitive_coping_alternative: Help the child generate alternative thoughts that are more accurate or helpful, in order to feel differently; discuss how to apply to real life
trauma_narrative: T: Therapist worked on a trauma narrative (TN) the child (GE)
trauma_narrative_rationale: Introduce rationale for TN; initiate TN (e.g. title page, timeline/table of contents)
trauma_narrative_details: Encourage child, in calibrated increments, to include more details of trauma
trauma_narrative_reread: Re-read the TN at the beginning of each session (GE)
trauma_narrative_add_thoughts: Ask about and add in thoughts and feelings throughout the TN
trauma_narrative_cognitive_processing: Use cognitive processing techniques to modify distortions throughout the TN
trauma_narrative_meaning: Include piece on making meaning (e.g. what they've learned, how they grew)
trauma_narrative_read_draft: As TN develops, read each new draft to supportive caregiver in collateral sessions
invivo_desensitization: I: Therapist developed in-vivo desensitization plan for generalized avoidant behaviors
child_parent: C: Conjoint child-parent session: sharing trauma narrative with parent/caregiver
child_parent_prepare: Prepare caregiver and child separately for joint session in which TN is shared
child_parent_joint_session: Hold joint session (e.g., re-read TN, model praise, discuss questions prepared by both child and caregiver, praise and celebrate progress made)
enhancing_safety: E: Therapist addressed child's sense of safety (e.g. safety skills and safety plan)
enhancing_safety_teach_skills: Teach personal safety skills and assertive communication; increase awareness
enhancing_safety_social_skills: Teach problem-solving skills and/or social skills as needed by the child
